findings.title: Closure merge never sheds a file a script stopped touching: 21 stale pairs force 1209 s of runs that cannot see the edit
findings.claim: tests/closure.py:_keep_committed_files keeps every committed closure entry a fresh recording omits, as long as the file still exists. On this tree, fresh `closure.py record` runs of 11 gate scripts omit, for files in this seat's cells, freq_control.py and log_latch.py (optimality, edge, validate, backtest) and repairs.py and silent_mode.py (boost_drift_replay, debug_collect, guard_pins, manual_plan, plan_view, solar_alignment, wood_advisor). merge --partial folds those records in and keeps all 21 pairs, and closure.select([F]) then puts the script in RUN for an edit to F, even though the script neither imports nor opens F. The lane tracer agrees: none of these runs executes a single line of those files, imports included. One edit to each of the four files forces 1209 s of recorded script time that cannot observe it. Outside the cells, inputs.py is stale in four of the solver scripts' entries in the same way.

findings.title: Scoped gate selects by file: 265 of 1423 selected runs import the edited module but run none of its function bodies
findings.claim: For a diff confined to function bodies of one production file in this seat's cells, tests/closure.py:select runs every script whose closure lists the file. In 265 of the 1423 (file, script) selections over the 65 cell files, the script's traced green run (the mutation lane's own tracer) imports the file but executes no line inside any of its function bodies and never reads it as text. The selected run therefore cannot observe the edit. The worst cases are boost_drift_replay.py (341 s recorded), forced by body edits to 19 cell files it only imports; optimality.py (142.5 s) by 6; backtest, edge and validate by 7 each; and env_drift.py, by the any-integration-change belt, for 19 files its --all capture only imports. Summed recorded seconds over these pairs: 7520 s, or about 116 s per one-file body edit, before counting env_drift's stub-recorded --all run. tests/mutation_table.py already skips such pairs (never_reaches) from the same traces. closure.select does not use them.

findings.title: features.py re-solves identical inputs: 60 main-process solves repeat one the same process already ran (exact, 3 runs)
findings.claim: In a green run of tests/features.py, 60 HeatPumpOptimizer.optimize calls made in the script's own process receive input that pickles byte-identically to a call that same process already solved. The pickle covers the optimizer's __dict__ and the call arguments. It also covers the identity of every function and class bound in every loaded heatpump_optimizer module and in the class dict, so a mock.patch or class swap between two calls makes them distinct. The 60 are exact across three runs on two machines (box B3 Linux: 113 total minus 53 worker-process repeats; orchestrator M1 macOS: 60 of 266 hashed with the atexit hook, and 148 total minus 88 worker repeats with the per-solve snapshot). The largest site is _r9egb9_transport, with 28 repeats from one call site (17-31 s CPU, provisional), followed by _lg_band (10, a helper called with identical arguments) and _r9f13_inline (8). On top of these, the coordinator's persistent process_worker child repeats at least 53 solves (88 when every worker's record survives), at about 72 s CPU. That count is a lower bound: a worker killed at shutdown before atexit lost its record under the original hook, and a worker restart resets its memory. Under the same key, tests/optimality.py has 0 repeats of 23 solves, and its patched re-solves are not counted. dst_checks.py has 0 of 116.

# D3-s3 REPORT (round 11, box B3, local re-run)

Findings: 3
- D3-s3-01 (low): Closure merge never sheds a file a script stopped touching: 21 stale pairs force 1209 s of runs that cannot see the edit
- D3-s3-02 (low): Scoped gate selects by file: 265 of 1423 selected runs import the edited module but run none of its function bodies
- D3-s3-03 (low): features.py re-solves identical inputs: 60 main-process solves repeat one the same process already ran (exact, 3 runs)

D3-s3-03 is keyed to the 60 main-process repeats. Box B3's total of 113 (60 main + 53 worker repeats) is a stated difference, not the key.

## Crash
Per-pair verdicts lost: prescreen_local.json/.progress.jsonl and prescreen_cheap.* were in the scratch clone under /private/tmp, cleared by the machine reboot at ~17:40Z. Attempt 3 (null control survived every driver, mutants from ~13:59Z) and the cheap-subset screen (from 16:24Z) produced verdicts that cannot be reported. The only verdict in the progress log, away.py:177 'killed' by entities.py at 16:58:57Z, fell in the ENOSPC window (~16:57Z) and is suspect, so it is not counted. examined=0 is the honest count.
